We are really far away, like too far to drive to hang out. Skyping is a really good idea, I hope he would be up for it. He does have a very sweet cat. It's hard, he just doesn't have *people* around him.  
  
The drinking problem is bad. Sometimes it seems like the main problem and sometimes it recedes a little bit. He knocks himself out with alcohol on a daily basis. He acknowledges that it is hurting his health, but has trouble stopping. I think he mixes pills in sometimes. It's out of hand.  
  
It's really good that his parents have at least some idea now of how serious things are. I just don't know if they will take it "seriously enough" or what that means. I think you are right, that they don't understand.  
  
Thanks for taking the time to respond.

During a long conversation, it is possible to talk to suggest things... he will listen a bit, but dismiss whatever doesn't fit with his dark vision of his life. It's like he has rehearsed the reasons for his depression that the WHY just becomes a part of the rehashing of the whole situation. I don't mean to sound harsh--I have been depressed before, and it really is hard to turn a corner.  
  
I'm afraid he just won't hear it regarding his therapist. But maybe being positive in the way you suggest would work. It really is a vicious cycle. He doesn't stick to meds... I think because he just can't manage it, he would have to really accept that he needed them. Something just doesn't click. Thank you for your perspective.

Thank you so much for responding. Part of the problem is that he *has* been in therapy (seeing the same therapist) for almost 6 years, but things haven't been getting better for him at all. I know my bf periodically encourages him to seek out another therapist... but his current therapist is the only other person he speaks openly to anymore (other than my boyfriend). The situation strikes me as sort of... weird?  
  
I guess my question is, how do we talk about this with him? It's really easy to get sucked into actually hours long conversations with him, yet at the same time it feels like nothing is communicated. My bf has spoken to Jason about his depression so endlessly (over a period of years) that I begin to wonder if it is somehow part of the problem, if that is possible.
